title: CEREBELLAR ATAXIA, IMPAIRED INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENT, AND DYSEQUILIBRIUM SYNDROME 4

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysequilibrium syndrome-4 (CAMRQ4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ATP8A2 gene (605870) on chromosome 13q12.13.

checks.claim: Cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysequilibrium syndrome-4 (CAMRQ4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ATP8A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Altogether, 6 of the 7 homozygous or compound heterozygous missense mutations known in ATP8A2 located in this subregion (amino acids 364‐877) of the catalytic cytoplasmic domain.
checks.explanation: The paper links CAMRQ4 to ATP8A2 mutations. It describes a homozygous variant in this family and compound heterozygous variants in earlier reports (Table 1).

checks.claim: The ATP8A2 gene is located on chromosome 13q12.13.
checks.evidence_quote: The ATP8A2 (OMIM 605 870) gene located at 13q12.1 that spans 653 878 bp and contains 37 exons.
checks.explanation: The paper gives 13q12.1. The draft's 13q12.13 is a sub-band within it, so the two agree; the more precise band is standard location nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: CAMRQ4 is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder (Mohamadian et al., 2020). Its features include cerebellar ataxia and impaired intellectual development, and some affected individuals show quadrupedal locomotion (Onat et al., 2013). Severe hypotonia and optic atrophy have also been reported in patients with ATP8A2 mutations (Mohamadian et al., 2020), as have athetotic involuntary movements (Narishige et al., 2022).

checks.claim: CAMRQ4 is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation, and dysequilibrium (CAMRQ) syndrome is a rare and early-onset neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.explanation: The paper also says: 'The pattern of inheritance in all of the possible phenotypes is autosomal recessive.'

checks.claim: Features of CAMRQ4 include cerebellar ataxia and impaired intellectual development.
checks.evidence_quote: Cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation and dysequilibrium syndrome is a rare and heterogeneous condition.
checks.explanation: The condition's name includes cerebellar ataxia and mental retardation (impaired intellectual development).

checks.claim: Some individuals affected by CAMRQ4 show quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.evidence_quote: Missense mutation in the ATPase, aminophospholipid transporter protein ATP8A2 is associated with cerebellar atrophy and quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.explanation: The title reports that quadrupedal locomotion is associated with the ATP8A2 mutation.

checks.claim: Severe hypotonia has been reported in patients with ATP8A2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: three additional patients in an Iranian consanguineous family with non-progressive cerebellar ataxia, severe hypotonia, intellectual disability, dysarthria, and cerebellar atrophy have been identified.
checks.explanation: The paper reports severe hypotonia in patients with an ATP8A2 mutation.

checks.claim: Optic atrophy has been reported in patients with ATP8A2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Besides, more severe phenotypes with optic atrophy, absence of ambulation, unhealthy brain MRI, non‐verbal or absent speech, and feeding difficulties have also been reported.
checks.explanation: The paper states that optic atrophy has been reported in CAMRQ4/ATP8A2 patients, and Table 1 shows it as well.

checks.claim: Athetotic involuntary movements have been reported in patients with ATP8A2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Japanese siblings presented with athetotic movements at 1 and 2 months of age.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes siblings with compound heterozygous ATP8A2 variants who had athetotic movements and other involuntary movements.

paragraphs.text: Onat et al. (2013) described a consanguineous family from Turkey with 4 affected individuals who had cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysequilibrium. The disorder in this family was associated with quadrupedal locomotion and cerebellar atrophy.

checks.claim: Onat et al. (2013) described a consanguineous family from Turkey with 4 affected individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated a consanguineous family from Turkey with four affected individuals exhibiting the condition.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The 4 affected individuals in the consanguineous Turkish family described by Onat et al. (2013) had cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysequilibrium.
checks.evidence_quote: Cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation and dysequilibrium syndrome is a rare and heterogeneous condition. We investigated a consanguineous family from Turkey with four affected individuals exhibiting the condition.
checks.explanation: The affected individuals have the condition, which consists of cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation and dysequilibrium.

checks.claim: The disorder in the consanguineous Turkish family described by Onat et al. (2013) was associated with quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.evidence_quote: Missense mutation in the ATPase, aminophospholipid transporter protein ATP8A2 is associated with cerebellar atrophy and quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.explanation: The title reports the association with quadrupedal locomotion.

checks.claim: The disorder in the consanguineous Turkish family described by Onat et al. (2013) was associated with cerebellar atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Missense mutation in the ATPase, aminophospholipid transporter protein ATP8A2 is associated with cerebellar atrophy and quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.explanation: The title reports the association with cerebellar atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Mohamadian et al. (2020) summarized the patients with ATP8A2 mutations reported by Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016). These patients had encephalopathy, impaired intellectual development, hypotonia, and optic atrophy.

checks.claim: Mohamadian et al. (2020) summarized the patients with ATP8A2 mutations reported by Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical data from affected members of the family compared with the previously reported patients with CAMRQ4 syndrome
checks.explanation: Table 1 includes a column for Martin‐Hernandez et al, 2016.

checks.claim: The patients with ATP8A2 mutations reported by Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) had encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Encephalopathy | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes
checks.explanation: Table 1 lists 'Yes' for encephalopathy in the Martin‐Hernandez et al, 2016 column (the fourth value in this row).

checks.claim: The patients with ATP8A2 mutations reported by Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) had impaired intellectual development.
checks.evidence_quote: Intellectual disability | Yes; IQ:20‐40 | Yes | Yes | Yes
checks.explanation: Table 1 lists 'Yes' for intellectual disability in the Martin‐Hernandez column.

checks.claim: The patients with ATP8A2 mutations reported by Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) had hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Hypotonia | Yes | Yes | No | Yes
checks.explanation: Table 1 lists 'Yes' for hypotonia in the Martin‐Hernandez column.

checks.claim: The patients with ATP8A2 mutations reported by Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) had optic atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Optic atrophy | No | No | ND | Yes
checks.explanation: Table 1 lists 'Yes' for optic atrophy in the Martin‐Hernandez column.

paragraphs.text: Mohamadian et al. (2020) stated that inheritance is autosomal recessive in all of the CAMRQ phenotypes. The family reported by Onat et al. (2013) was consanguineous, and the disorder in that family was mapped by homozygosity mapping.

checks.claim: Mohamadian et al. (2020) stated that inheritance is autosomal recessive in all of the CAMRQ phenotypes.
checks.evidence_quote: The pattern of inheritance in all of the possible phenotypes is autosomal recessive.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly in the introduction about CAMRQ.

checks.claim: The CAMRQ family reported by Onat et al. (2013) was consanguineous.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated a consanguineous family from Turkey with four affected individuals exhibiting the condition.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the family was consanguineous.

checks.claim: The disorder in the family reported by Onat et al. (2013) was mapped by homozygosity mapping.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity mapping revealed that several shared homozygous regions, including chromosome 13q12.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that homozygosity mapping was performed.

paragraphs.text: Onat et al. (2013) noted an unrelated individual whose impaired intellectual development and severe hypotonia were associated with a de novo balanced t(10; 13) translocation that disrupted ATP8A2. Mohamadian et al. (2020) stated that this translocation interrupted the ATP8A2 coding sequence.

checks.claim: Onat et al. (2013) noted an individual, unrelated to the CAMRQ family, with impaired intellectual development and severe hypotonia associated with a de novo balanced t(10;13) translocation.
checks.evidence_quote: an unrelated individual has been identified, in whom mental retardation and severe hypotonia is associated with a de novo t(10;13) balanced translocation resulting with the disruption of ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The de novo balanced t(10;13) translocation noted by Onat et al. (2013) disrupted the ATP8A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a de novo t(10;13) balanced translocation resulting with the disruption of ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the translocation disrupted ATP8A2.

checks.claim: Mohamadian et al. (2020) stated that the t(10;13) translocation interrupted the ATP8A2 coding sequence.
checks.evidence_quote: In the first study, a de novo balanced translocation t(10;13) interrupting the ATP8A2 coding sequence was detected in a patient with major axial hypotonia and moderate intellectual disability.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Onat et al. (2013) studied a consanguineous Turkish family with CAMRQ. Homozygosity mapping showed several shared homozygous regions, including chromosome 13q12. Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual, followed by segregation analysis, identified a missense mutation in the ATP8A2 gene, I376M. The mutation segregated with the disorder in the family.

checks.claim: Onat et al. (2013) studied a consanguineous Turkish family with CAMRQ.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated a consanguineous family from Turkey with four affected individuals exhibiting the condition.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Homozygosity mapping in the consanguineous Turkish CAMRQ family studied by Onat et al. (2013) showed several shared homozygous regions, including chromosome 13q12.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity mapping revealed that several shared homozygous regions, including chromosome 13q12.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual from the Turkish CAMRQ family, followed by segregation analysis, identified the I376M missense mutation in the ATP8A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual followed by segregation analysis, population screening and prediction approaches revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The ATP8A2 I376M mutation segregated with the disorder in the consanguineous Turkish CAMRQ family.
checks.evidence_quote: Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual followed by segregation analysis, population screening and prediction approaches revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: The abstract says a segregation analysis was done and the variant was reported as causal, which implies segregation. It does not state the segregation result outright. The identical claim av0001.1#3 was judged supported on the same reasoning, so the two verdicts should be made consistent.

paragraphs.text: Onat et al. (2013) studied a consanguineous Turkish family with CAMRQ4 and quadrupedal locomotion. Homozygosity mapping was followed by targeted sequencing, and in this family they identified an ile376-to-met (I376M) missense mutation in the ATP8A2 gene. The mutation segregated with the disorder.

checks.claim: Onat et al. (2013) studied a consanguineous Turkish family with CAMRQ4 and quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated a consanguineous family from Turkey with four affected individuals exhibiting the condition.
checks.explanation: The family is described in the abstract, and the title links the mutation to quadrupedal locomotion.

checks.claim: In the consanguineous Turkish CAMRQ4 family, homozygosity mapping followed by targeted sequencing identified an ile376-to-met (I376M) missense mutation in the ATP8A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual followed by segregation analysis, population screening and prediction approaches revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: Homozygosity mapping followed by targeted sequencing identified p.I376M.

checks.claim: The ATP8A2 I376M mutation segregated with the disorder in the consanguineous Turkish CAMRQ4 family.
checks.evidence_quote: Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual followed by segregation analysis, population screening and prediction approaches revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: The variant came out of a segregation analysis and was reported as the cause, which implies it segregated with the disorder.
